correctness.rationale: For fixed u with annihilator g and d=deg(g), the determinant lemma reduces the target to a linear equation in v. The coefficient vectors of g(t)(tI-A)^(-1)u form a triangular basis of the cyclic span of u,Au,...,A^(d-1)u. Thus the image is all (chi_A/g) times polynomials of degree <d, with q^(n-d) lifts per target, including u=0 by the zero-dimensional convention. Primary exponent e has precisely K_e-K_(e-1) choices by the kernel dimensions of the f-power maps; divisibility by chi_A/g gives exactly the lower limits r_f, and summation factors. Every nonzero rank-one matrix has q-1 factorizations and zero has 2q^n-1, giving the correction. At the unchanged target the summation-by-parts coefficients on the kernel sizes before stabilization are strictly positive. Indeed sum_j min(e,lambda_j) equals M minus max_r(sum_(j<=r) lambda_j - re), so dominance gives the stated direction; distinct partitions have different increments of these dimensions, ensuring strictness somewhere before M. Rank-one extremes follow from a single irreducible factor or from the scalar dot-product count. These arguments work in characteristic two and in dimension one as well. Independent finite checks used direct determinant expansion and literal updates for 92 targets across 13 types over F_2 and F_3, plus 699 exact partition comparisons for q=2,3,5 and partition size up to seven. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/2dcda91d-ea99-4105-aaf8-f8900e12579b/independent_fiber_check.py. Those checks are bounded and do not establish the theorem for general q or n.

evidence: The arbitrary-field rank <= m theorem requires, for each eigenvalue, target multiplicity at least the algebraic multiplicity minus the total size of the m largest Jordan blocks. The earlier rank-one theorem likewise addresses existence. Hansmann addresses prescribed spectral configurations for complex operators, not finite-field multiplicities at a fixed A.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For m=1 over a finite field, separability identifies the eigenvalue condition with nu_f(theta)>=M_f-L_f; since that power divides chi_A, this is exactly nu_f(chi_A-theta)>=M_f-L_f. This covers positivity of the ordered-pair fiber, not its size or the size after subtraction of the zero update at the unchanged target.

evidence: The determinant identity linearizes the target for fixed u, and existence identifies support. The proof must still group u by all its primary annihilator exponents and sum different compatible-covector weights. Strict dominance additionally needs positivity of the summation-by-parts weights and comparison of the kernel profiles.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Feasibility alone supplies no cardinalities and cannot distinguish isospectral fibers, all of which contain the zero update. Fixed-input placement does not by itself account for the distribution of cyclic subspaces as u varies. The standard linearization and fixed-u counting are not credited as new.
searches: Ran–Wojtylak Proposition 2.2; Merzel et al. Theorems 1 and 2; fixed-input pole placement, doi:10.1002/mma.8240

evidence: Ran–Wojtylak give the rank-one resolvent/characteristic-polynomial identity in the complex setting. The Resultary rank-one Fourier result 2cad679e45a7 sums a squarefree target class at rank-one frequencies, not a translated rank-one update set at fixed A.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: In the additive matrix group the update count is a convolution with the rank-one sphere, plus the zero-update contribution for ordered pairs. Knowing the target's Fourier coefficients only at rank-one frequencies is not that pointwise convolution, and the squarefree restriction does not include the varying primary partitions of the dominance theorem.

value.rationale: The exact fiber size gives the probability of each characteristic polynomial under uniform factorized rank-one updates, or under uniform distinct nonzero rank-one updates after correction. The unchanged-target counts also strictly detect comparable changes in the primary partitions that the support condition cannot distinguish. These are motivated finite-field statistics for arbitrary input matrices, not just an extra test of a known attainability criterion.
